Cloverdale's town centre sits at the crossroads of Highway 10 and Highway 15 (Pacific Highway / 176 Street).
The July 22, 2024 plan expansion runs from 60 Avenue south to 64 Avenue north, between 175 / 175A Street west and 180 Street east, plus one lot at 18120 56 Avenue.
The Cloverdale Fairgrounds are a separate Special Study Area, not inside the Town Centre Plan's scope.
The plan area mixes commercial, industrial and residential neighbourhoods around a pedestrian-oriented core on 176 Street.
Schools confirmed by address include Cloverdale Traditional at 17857 56 Avenue, A.J. McLellan Elementary at 16545 61 Avenue and Lord Tweedsmuir Secondary at 6151 180 Street.
The local rule is heritage form on 176 Street: the Town Centre Plan's urban design guidelines maintain 2-storey building heights on 176 Street inside the Heritage Character Area.

The Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) edges the community's lowland side; for ALR parcels the Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) frame is one principal residence of at most 500 square metres plus at most one additional residence.
The Town Centre Plan update includes a review of sensitive ecosystems and riparian areas, which can reclassify land near creeks.

blocks.text: Cloverdale: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Downtown Cloverdale is described by the City as the historical centre of Surrey, with a heritage character area extended north along 176 Street to 58A Avenue.
Existing surface parking lots on 176A Street were preserved in the plan after open-house input, a detail that affects core redevelopment parcels.
One lot northeast of the Kwantlen Polytechnic University Tech campus, at 18120 56 Avenue, was added to the plan expansion on its own, outside the main rectangle.

Full entry for this cluster: the Cloverdale Town Centre Plan update itself, endorsed October 30, 2023 and boundary-expanded July 22, 2024, is at Step 3, developing the plan update, refining land use, parks and transportation options.

The local angle is plan contributions: the City states that when new development occurs in an area with a land use plan, the developer must make contributions toward public facilities and upgrade sidewalks.
Two provincial highways cross here: Highway 10 (56 Avenue) east-west and Highway 15 (176 Street / Pacific Highway) north-south toward the Pacific Highway border crossing.
Check creek-adjacent lots against the plan update's sensitive ecosystems and riparian review, which the City states may identify new areas or reclassify existing ones.
Check lowland-edge parcels for Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status on Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) mapping before assuming a second dwelling or a non-farm use is permitted.

faq.q: Is Cloverdale its own city, or part of Surrey?
faq.a: Part of Surrey — Cloverdale is one of the seven communities on the City of Surrey's Our Communities page, described by the City as its historic centre and its third largest community, with Langley to the east and Guildford and Fleetwood to the north.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Cloverdale?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 158 houses listed with 26 sold in the month and 105 condos and townhomes listed with 11 sold in the month in Cloverdale. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Cloverdale a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 16%, a balanced market; condos and townhomes had a sales ratio of 10%, a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
